reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: A type II collagenopathy caused by dominant COL2A1 variants, part of a spectrum that also includes achondrogenesis type II, spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia congenita and Stickler syndrome
Features disproportionate short stature with a short trunk and short limbs, prominent enlarged joints with restricted movement, and progressive contractures
Craniofacial features include a round flat face, midface hypoplasia, prominent eyes and cleft palate in many patients
Ocular involvement (high myopia, retinal detachment, cataract) reflects the shared type II collagen defect and requires ophthalmological surveillance
Sensorineural or conductive hearing loss and recurrent otitis media are common
Radiographs show dumbbell-shaped femora, platyspondyly with coronal clefts, and characteristic large 'swiss-cheese' cartilage on histology
Overlap with other COL2A1 disorders means phenotype and severity vary; the tell-tale combination is stiff enlarged joints plus ocular and hearing problems
reference.pathophysiology: Kniest dysplasia arises from dominant-negative variants in COL2A1, encoding the alpha-1 chain of type II collagen, the principal collagen of cartilage, the vitreous and the nucleus pulposus. Most are in-frame exon-skipping or splice variants that yield a shortened but incorporated collagen chain, disrupting the fibril network throughout cartilaginous tissues. The abnormal matrix produces soft, vacuolated cartilage (the histological 'swiss-cheese' appearance), leading to defective endochondral ossification, joint stiffness and the ocular and auditory manifestations shared across the type II collagenopathies.
additionalInvestigations: Skeletal survey documenting dumbbell femora, platyspondyly and coronal vertebral clefts
Ophthalmological assessment including dilated retinal examination for myopia and detachment risk
Audiometry and ENT review for hearing loss and middle-ear disease
Cervical spine imaging to assess odontoid hypoplasia and instability
redFlags: Symptoms of retinal detachment (flashes, floaters, field loss) demanding urgent ophthalmology review
Cervical instability with odontoid hypoplasia before anaesthesia or manipulation
Progressive respiratory compromise from restrictive chest and airway involvement
Cleft palate with feeding or airway difficulties in infancy
reference.prognosis: Survival is generally good, but morbidity from progressive joint stiffness, contractures, myopia with retinal detachment risk, and hearing loss is substantial. Lifelong multidisciplinary surveillance mitigates avoidable complications.
pitfalls: Labelling the disorder purely as a skeletal problem and neglecting mandatory eye and hearing surveillance
Missing retinal detachment because myopia was assumed to be simple refractive error
Overlooking cervical instability prior to airway management
Confusing Kniest with metatropic dysplasia given historical naming and radiographic overlap

GeneReviews: Type II Collagen Disorders Overview
management: Ophthalmological surveillance with dilated retinal examination and prompt treatment of high myopia, cataract and retinal detachment, as there is no disease-specific therapy
Audiological monitoring and management of hearing loss and recurrent otitis media with grommets and hearing aids
Physiotherapy and orthopaedic care for joint stiffness, contractures and progressive deformity, with joint replacement in adulthood
Cervical spine imaging with anaesthetic and activity precautions for odontoid hypoplasia and instability
Cleft palate repair with feeding and speech support
Pain management for progressive joint disease
Genetic counselling reflecting dominant COL2A1 inheritance, often arising de novo
